Action Plan:
1. Suspected contact dermatitis of the palms likely related to cleaning products:
   - Advise strict avoidance of irritants; wear protective gloves at all times when cleaning.
   - Prescribe topical steroid cream (specific agent/potency not documented); apply as prescribed for approximately 10–14 days.
   - Prescribe stronger emollients; apply liberally 3–4 times daily for the next 1–2 weeks.
   - Follow up in 10–14 days if not improving, or sooner if symptoms worsen or spread.
   - Prescription to be sent electronically to the patient’s pharmacy.
2. Type 2 diabetes:
   - Continue current therapy (metformin; dose/route/frequency not documented). No changes discussed today.
Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: Painful, cracked skin on hands with itching.
- History of present illness:
  - Onset: ~3–4 months ago.
  - Location: Palms predominately.
  - Course: Worsened recently; now painful and impacting work; took 3 days off work.
  - Symptoms: Dryness, cracking, itching; occasional bleeding when scratched; no spontaneous bleeding reported.
  - Associated: Mild generalized dry skin on legs (longstanding, not severe).
  - Systemic symptoms: Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, bowel or urinary issues; appetite and general well-being maintained.
  - Potential triggers: Housekeeping work using cleaning products; inconsistent glove use; new hotel job started ~4 months ago; more product use in bathrooms.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. No known eczema or dermatitis diagnosed previously. No asthma or bowel problems reported.
- Medications:
  - Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - OTC tried: E45 emollient — dose/route/frequency not documented; no benefit.
  - OTC tried: Antihistamine — name/dose/route/frequency not documented; no benefit.
- Allergies: No known drug or general allergies.
- Family history: Diabetes; no known skin disorders.
- Social history:
  - Occupation: Housekeeper in a hotel; inconsistent glove use.
  - Tobacco: Non-smoker.
  - Alcohol: A couple of pints per week.

Objective:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Physical exam: Not documented.
- Investigations: None performed or ordered today.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Hand dermatitis (contact dermatitis of the palms):
   - Assessment: Likely irritant contact dermatitis related to cleaning chemicals and inconsistent glove use.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Avoid triggers/irritants; wear protective gloves consistently while cleaning.
     - Topical steroid cream prescribed (specific agent/potency/dose not documented) for approximately 10–14 days.
     - Stronger emollients prescribed; apply 3–4 times daily for 1–2 weeks.
     - Prescription sent to pharmacy.
   - Follow-up: Reassess in 10–14 days if not improved; return sooner if symptoms worsen or spread.
   - Referrals: None discussed.

2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus:
   - Assessment: Known T2DM.
   - Treatment planned: Continue metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented). No changes discussed.
   - Follow-up: Routine diabetes management not addressed in this visit.
